text:
maria: Heads-up — nightly CI flagged a regression in the kernel candidate set we landed yesterday. Seen on Ampere A10G, seq_len=2048 workload.

maria: CI job: kernel-probe-ci/1769123456. Summary from perf-bot below, latency increased ~18% on the long-seq microbench for kern_x8_q4.

perf-bot: [auto-report] 1769123456: kern_x8_q4 | ampere-a10g | seq=2048 | bs=1 | tokens/sec: 678 -> 558 (-17.7%) | p50: 12.3ms -> 14.6ms | p99: 45.2ms -> 61.8ms

alex: ack. Curious if this is KV-cache warmup or actual kernel math change. Any traces from perf viewer?

liz: I pulled a flamegraph from the microbench run. Looks like memcpy and transposes spiked. KV cache hit-rate is fine (~99%), but the memory layout path for long sequences picks a different transpose kernel (transpose_tiled_v2).

liz: snippet from perf viewer:
```
# top stacks (seq=2048, bs=1)
25% memcpy_device_to_host
18% transpose_tiled_v2
12% matmul_q4_kern_x8
8% kernel_dispatch_overhead
```

jon: that transpose_tiled_v2 was added to favor smaller blocks on A10G to reduce L2 thrash. But for seq=2048 it may be thrashing caches because of our KV layout (interleaved heads). Could explain p99 jump.

alex: we need an isolated microbench run across kernels + seq sweep. Maria can you drop the exact command used by the CI probe? I'll reproduce locally.

maria: CI runs the harness: `./tools/kernel_probe --kernels all_candidates.json --arch ampere-a10g --seqs 32,128,512,1024,1536,2048 --bs 1 --repeat 50 --out /tmp/ci-run-1769123456.json`

maria: Here's the relevant excerpt from the CI artifact: `kernel:kern_x8_q4, seq=2048, avg_latency_ms=14.6, stdev=2.3, tokens_s=558`

jon: can you also try forcing the old transpose (transpose_tiled_v1) in the harness? Might be a regression in the new tiled path. We can compare memory throughput counters.

liz: ran local reproducer with env override `TRANSPOSE_IMPL=transpose_tiled_v1`:
```
$ TRANSPOSE_IMPL=transpose_tiled_v1 ./tools/kernel_probe --kernel kern_x8_q4 --arch ampere-a10g --seq 2048 --bs 1 --repeat 100
avg p50: 12.4ms | p99: 47.1ms | tokens/s: 675
```

liz: so swapping transpose impl recovers baseline. That suggests autotuner or kernel selector prefers tiled_v2 for this arch/seq, which is wrong for long seqs.

perf-bot: added regression label to ticket RW-PLT-3482 and uploaded artifact link: https://ci.redwood.internal/artifacts/1769123456/kernel-probe.json

alex: two follow-ups: 1) change autotuner heuristic to consider sequence length when ranking transpose kernels (long-locality -> prefer v1), 2) add microbenchmark for transpose impls into nightly sweep for seq >= 1024.

jon: +1. Also add a PSV (per-sequence-variance) metric to the CI check so we catch p99 regressions, not just mean tokens/sec. Many regressions show up in tails.

maria: I'll open a PR with the autotuner patch to bias transpose selection for seq >= 1024 on Ampere. Draft name: "autotune: prefer transpose_v1 for long sequences on ampere".

maria: PR link (draft): https://git.redwood/infr/runtime/pulls/2389

liz: also suggest we expand the kernel_probe harness to emit NVTX ranges and memory bandwidth counters so SRE can triage faster. Minimal change: add `--nvtx` and `--memstats` flags.

alex: good idea. For CI: make the nightly sweep run the transpose microbench with these flags and fail if p99 regressed >10% vs baseline.

perf-bot: note: baseline set created on 1767000000, arch-specific baselines exist for ampere-a10g. Will compute new baselines after PR merges.

maria: re-run planned locally and in canary CI after PR. Command I'll use for canary:
```
TRANSPOSE_IMPL=auto ./tools/kernel_probe --kernels all_candidates.json --arch ampere-a10g --seqs 32,128,512,1024,1536,2048 --bs 1 --nvtx --memstats --repeat 100 --out /tmp/canary.json
```

jon: if canary passes, we should also apply a guard in the runtime: when seq >= 1024 and arch==ampere-a10g, prefer transpose_v1 unless autotuner has 95%+ confidence in v2. Safer fallback.

alex: agreed. We'll add the runtime fallback as a hotfix if CI shows further noise.

maria: OK starting work. Will post updates here with artifact links and CI numbers. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Job kernel-probe-ci/1769123456 rerun queued by @maria. ETA ~12m.

maria: tiny note — we should also add a small memcopy microbench to distinguish memcpy throughput regressions vs transpose logic. Today's flamegraph showed memcpy climb.

liz: added to follow-up checklist in RW-PLT-3482.

alex: great thread. Keep it tight. If anyone hits more regressions, ping #incidents.
